title: A Friendly Face: Do Text-to-Image Systems Rely on Stereotypes when the Input is Under-Specified?
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured stereotypical associations between social traits and perceived demographics in generated images. Specifically for religion, it measured whether prompts for a 'religious' person resulted in images with stereotypical demographic characteristics (skin color, gender, age) compared to prompts for a 'science-oriented' person.
findings: Prompts containing the word 'religious' (as opposed to 'science-oriented') showed stereotypical associations. In Midjourney and Stable Diffusion, 'religious' was significantly associated with darker-skinned subjects. In DALL-E and Stable Diffusion, 'religious' was associated with older-aged subjects. The findings suggest these models have learned and reproduce visual stereotypes associating religiosity with specific demographic groups.
